reason: A graph built from one bundle's records converts to a document that declares only the ex prefix and the default namespace of the bundle's document. The docstring of `graph_to_prov`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says the new document declares what the first record's document declares.

A bundle with its own default namespace converts to a graph and back to the flattened, unified document, with the bundle's default declared under the prefix dn. `docs/howto/networkx.md` says a bundle's own default namespace is declared under a prefix, as `ProvDocument.flattened` declares it.

A document with a wasGeneratedBy and an influence between declared elements converts with ProvWarning turned into an error, and gives two edges. The skip rule in the docstring of `prov_to_graph` warns only for an unset or uninferrable endpoint, and this test guards against over-warning.
Two equal memberships that share ex:m draw one edge in the graph. #548 and the 3.3.0 entry in `HISTORY.md` say `unified` keeps each record once, so `prov_to_graph` draws one edge.

A hand-built graph of records from two documents with different default namespaces, with or without a top-level record of the second, converts to records that keep their IRIs. The docstring of `graph_to_prov`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says it declares a prefix for every other default namespace that a record's bundle or document reads.

A hand-built graph of records from one default-namespace bundle, a document and a bundle, or two bundles, in either order, converts to records that keep their IRIs. The docstring of `graph_to_prov`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says it declares a prefix for every other default namespace that a record's bundle or document reads, which `graph_to_prov` does through `ProvDocument._declare_prefixes_for_bundle_defaults`. The judge ruled to remove the row `one-bundle-reversed`, and the maintainer declined. That row builds the same graph as `one-bundle-in-order`, because reversing a one-element tuple changes nothing (the verifier printed both rows' graphs). A fault that passes `scopes[1:]` to `ProvDocument._declare_prefixes_for_bundle_defaults` in `graph_to_prov` fails `one-bundle-in-order` with the row deselected. The row stays because the test draws its rows as the product of two parametrize decorators, and dropping one row means writing out the other five, which makes the test eleven lines longer.

`graph_to_prov` of a graph with nodes a and b and one edge returns a document with no records, whether the edge has no relation key (row `no-relation-key`) or a relation that is not a ProvRecord (row `not-a-record`). The docstring of `graph_to_prov`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says an edge is added only when its relation data is a ProvRecord. Merged from `test_graphs.py::test_ignores_edges_without_relation_key` and `test_graphs.py::test_ignores_edges_whose_relation_is_not_a_prov_record`. The two bodies differed only in the edge's keyword arguments, which `**edge_data` passes unchanged, and both rows reach the one check in `graph_to_prov` where `edge_data.get("relation")` gives None or a string. Each row keeps its input and its assertion, and the verifier's planted faults show each row catching its own shape. A subscript read of the relation fails `no-relation-key` and not `not-a-record`, and a None check in place of the `ProvRecord` check fails `not-a-record` and not `no-relation-key`.

Folded into `test_graphs.py::test_graph_to_prov_ignores_an_edge_whose_relation_is_not_a_prov_record` as row `not-a-record` (edge data `{"relation": "not-a-record"}`), with the same graph, call and assertion. `graph_to_prov` adds an edge only when its relation is a ProvRecord, and a fault that tests for None in place of that type check fails that row and not the other.

Folded into `test_graphs.py::test_graph_to_prov_ignores_an_edge_whose_relation_is_not_a_prov_record` as row `no-relation-key` (edge data `{}`), with the same graph, call and assertion. `graph_to_prov` reads the edge's relation with `edge_data.get("relation")`, and a fault that reads it with a subscript fails that row and not the other.

`graph_to_prov` of a graph with a string node and an inferred entity that has no bundle returns a document with no records. The docstring of `graph_to_prov`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says only a ProvRecord node that has a bundle is added.

An entity ex:e in two bundles, with ex:v in one and ex:w in the other, gives one node that holds both attributes. The docstring of `prov_to_graph`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says records that share an identifier across its bundles are merged, as #651 asks.

Two associations that share ex:assoc1 and differ on `prov:plan` raise ProvUnificationError with "an absent prov:plan means none" from `prov_to_graph`, in one scope and across two bundles. The docstring of `prov_to_graph`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says ProvUnificationError propagates from `unified`, and `docs/howto/networkx.md` says so too.

`prov_to_graph` raises TypeError "must be a ProvDocument, not ProvBundle" for a bundle and "not NoneType" for None. The docstring of `prov_to_graph`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, lists the TypeError, and `docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md` gives the message for a bundle (#651).

A generation inside a bundle that names a top-level activity gives two declared nodes, one edge and the flattened, unified document on the way back, with DeprecationWarning from prov as an error. #651 and `docs/howto/networkx.md` say `prov_to_graph` flattens the document, so the records of every bundle are included.

A wasGeneratedBy between undeclared ex:e2 and ex:a2 gives one ProvEntity node, one ProvActivity node, no bundle on either node and one edge. The docstring of `prov_to_graph` says an undeclared endpoint becomes a bare node of the inferred class, and the docstring of `graph_to_prov` says a node without a bundle is a bare inferred node.

A generation with no activity gives no edge and one ProvWarning that matches Generation. The docstring of `prov_to_graph`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says a relation with an unset endpoint is skipped with a ProvWarning, and `docs/howto/networkx.md` repeats it.

A wasInfluencedBy between undeclared names is dropped with one ProvWarning that matches Influence, and the later generation still gives two nodes and one edge. The docstring of `prov_to_graph`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, says a relation whose undeclared endpoint type cannot be inferred is skipped with a ProvWarning.

A wasDerivedFrom between two undeclared names under a default namespace converts to a graph and back to a document that equals the unified original and keeps its default namespace. `docs/howto/networkx.md` says `graph_to_prov` reverses the conversion, and its docstring says the new document declares what the first record's document declares.

For every canonical example document, `graph_to_prov` of `prov_to_graph` gives the records of the flattened, unified document that have both endpoints set. The docstrings of `prov_to_graph` and `graph_to_prov`, rendered by `docs/reference/graph.md`, and `docs/howto/networkx.md` say the graph holds the flattened, unified records and converts back, as #651 asks.
